title: clean
notes: THE OUTLIER. At $16,500 this is roughly $4,300 under the median for the spec, fully equipped, clean title. Price has already dropped $1,495 from $17,995 back in December, so it has been sitting. Explanations on the listing: an accident is reported and there are multiple previous owners — but neither obviously accounts for that big a discount. The listing also says 'seller has not disclosed fees', which at an independent lot is worth taking literally. Your own criteria say to investigate cars this cheap, so treat it as a lead to verify rather than a bargain to grab. DEEP-DIVE 2026-09-19 - the cheapness is now explained. Three things, none of them hidden. (1) An accident is REPORTED and there are multiple owners. (2) It has been on this lot since 23 DEC 2025 - roughly nine months - and has been marked down twice: $17,995 to $16,995 in March, then to $16,500 on 28 Aug. (3) The listing says "Seller has not disclosed fees", and Arizona does not cap doc fees, so the $18,664 out-the-door figure here assumes the $599 default and could be materially wrong. The nine months is the important one: a complete-spec CR-V at $16,500 in Phoenix should not sit unsold that long, so something is putting buyers off in person or on the CarFax. That is either the best lever on this board or the reason to walk. VIN decodes clean as EX-L with the L15BE 1.5L turbo - the oil-dilution engine, which Phoenix heat mitigates but does not eliminate. SOLD/DELISTED, confirmed 2026-09-22: cars.com returns "Sorry, this vehicle is no longer available". After 272 days and two markdowns it finally went, at $16,500 with the reported accident never explained. It had been the cheapest complete CR-V on the board by roughly $2,000 and the benchmark every other car was measured against. That comparison is now gone.
checks: ASK THE FEE QUESTION FIRST, before anything else: get the itemised out-the-door number in writing. "Seller has not disclosed fees" on an independent lot in a state with no doc-fee cap is where a $16,500 car becomes an $18,500 car.
Ask why it has been on the lot since December. Listen to the answer.
CarFax specifically for accident SEVERITY and whether structural/frame was hit - "reported" alone tells you nothing
Recall 26V332000 (May 2026): front passenger seat weight sensor can crack and cause unintended airbag deployment in a crash. Very recent - likely UNREPAIRED. Check by VIN.
Recall 23V858000: fuel pump can fail and stall the engine while driving
Recall 18V663000: electric power steering magnet can dislodge and apply assist the WRONG WAY during a full-lock turn
Recall 23V158000: front seat belt buckle may fail to latch
1.5L turbo oil dilution: pull the dipstick and SMELL it for fuel, check the oil level is not ABOVE full, and ask for oil-change records
Free NICB VINCheck and a ~$4 NMVTIS report before spending anything on an inspection
Call any Phoenix Honda dealer with the VIN for the full factory service history
Independent pre-purchase inspection, not the selling dealer's
FIND OUT WHY IT IS THIS CHEAP — $4.3k under median with no stated reason
Pull the CarFax yourself; do not accept a dealer-printed summary
Ask directly: has this car ever been a rental, fleet, or auction vehicle?
Get every fee in writing up front — the listing explicitly does not disclose them
It has been listed since at least December — ask why it has not sold

notes: A GOOD CAR IN THE WRONG BUDGET. Out the door this is $26,498 against a $20,000 target - over by $6,498, and past the $23,000 ceiling on sticker alone. Nothing wrong with the car: 50,256 miles is the second-lowest of any CR-V tracked, it is three years newer than anything else on the board, the feature set is complete with nothing to retrofit, and it is 0 accidents on a clean title. VIN confirms EX-L, L15BE 1.5 turbo, FWD, built in Alliston. Cars.com calls it a Great Deal at $734 under the $25,033 average, and that is probably fair - the problem is not that this car is overpriced, it is that 2021 EX-Ls cost more than the budget. Useful as a price-tier marker: against the Fine Cars 2018 EX it is $5,813 more out the door for three years newer and 30,239 fewer miles. WATCH THE ADD-ONS: the listing offers "complimentary benefits valued at up to $1,167" - concierge, GPS theft protection, ceramic coating, nitrogen fill. Those are usually pre-installed dealer profit items with the cost already inside the asking price rather than genuine gifts, and nitrogen fill is worth nothing. Ask whether the price falls if you decline them. Price was cut $2,042 TODAY, 19 days after listing, so it is moving. AUTOCHECK 2026-09-22 - CLEAN, and the reassuring kind of clean. TWO owners, not an unknown number: owner 1 bought it new in Yuma on 26 Apr 2021 and kept it three years (~9,500 mi/yr); owner 2 in Mesa from Jun 2024 (~9,700 mi/yr). Both personal use, both Arizona, no fleet, rental or lease. No accidents, no damage, airbags never deployed, no structural damage. Clean title, no brands. Five odometer readings from the MVD, two dealer listings and an emissions test all line up, with no rollback. Passed Arizona emissions 18 May 2026. That settles the 'multiple owners' worry raised earlier: it is two ordinary owners. The in-service date also confirms the factory warranty point - Honda's 5yr/60k powertrain coverage ran out 26 Apr 2026. Two small open items: (1) liens were recorded for both owners, three times for owner 2 in 2024, which usually means a refinance - a dealer has to deliver clear title, but confirm the lien release is done; (2) it is at 50,256 miles, right at Honda's 50k service - ask whether Courtesy did it. The report shows no service records at all, so call a Honda dealer with the VIN; owner 2 was in Mesa, so the history is probably at a local Honda store.
checks: Confirm the lien from the previous owner has been released and Courtesy can deliver a clear title - AutoCheck shows liens recorded in 2024
Ask whether the 50,000-mile service was done: oil and filter, engine air filter, tire rotation, brake inspection. If not, ask them to do it before delivery
Call a Honda dealer (a Mesa one is likely) with the VIN for the service history - AutoCheck shows none
ASK WHETHER THE PRICE DROPS IF YOU DECLINE the $1,167 of "complimentary" add-ons - concierge, GPS theft protection, ceramic coating, nitrogen fill
Get the out-the-door number in writing; $699 doc is at the high end
Cut $2,042 today after 19 days. It may not be finished falling.
1.5L turbo oil dilution: smell the dipstick, check oil is not above full
Check open recalls by VIN, including 26V332000 (seat weight sensor)
Free NICB VINCheck and a ~$4 NMVTIS report before paying for an inspection
Call any Phoenix Honda dealer with the VIN for the free factory service history
Independent pre-purchase inspection, not the selling dealer's

title: clean
notes: THE HIGHER-BUDGET SWEEP FOUND THIS AND IT BEATS THE COURTESY KIA CR-V ON EVERY AXIS AT LESS MONEY. Out the door roughly $26,370 against $26,778 for the 2021 CR-V EX-L - so $400 CHEAPER, two years newer, 16,256 fewer miles, and ALL-WHEEL DRIVE where the CR-V is front-wheel. For 2023 Mazda made AWD and the full i-ACTIVSENSE suite standard on every CX-5 including this base 2.5 S: radar cruise, blind-spot, rear cross-traffic, smart brake support, lane keep, CarPlay and Android Auto all confirmed on the listing. The powertrain point matters most: this is the naturally aspirated 2.5, which CRITERIA.md lists as having NO KNOWN life-limiting fault and a 200-260k ceiling, against the CR-V's 1.5 turbo and its oil-dilution history. Seats are CLOTH, which is the thing the leather conversation was looking for. CarMax terms: no doc fee, 30-day limited warranty, 10-day money back, and it is sitting at Phoenix-West Valley available today. What it gives up against the CR-V EX-L is leather, moonroof, power liftgate, heated seats and memory seats - comfort, not safety and not longevity.
checks: Confirm the $23,998 is genuinely all-in - CarMax advertises no doc fee in Arizona, so verify tax and registration are the only additions
Free reservation is available - hold it before driving out
Confirm heated seats: base 2.5 S may not have them (Preferred adds them). Less of an issue in Phoenix.
Get the CarMax detailed history report and read the accident line
Check open recalls by VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls
Use the 10-day money back window as the real safety net, but still get an independent inspection rather than relying on it
Free NICB VINCheck and a ~$4 NMVTIS report

title: clean
notes: THE BETTER VERSION OF THE CR-V YOU WANT. Found comparing Courtesy Kia's 2021 EX-L against every other Arizona CR-V at the same money. One owner, zero accidents, clean title, 39,862 miles - against Courtesy's MULTIPLE owners and 50,256 miles - and $1,103 less on sticker. 2020 and 2021 are the same car: 2020 was the mid-cycle refresh, 2021 carried it over, both on the 1.5 turbo with full Honda Sensing. So the extra year at Courtesy buys one Phoenix summer of calendar age and nothing else. EX not EX-L, which means CLOTH, heated seats, moonroof and remote start but no leather, power liftgate or memory seat. The cloth is what was wanted anyway. EchoPark Phoenix is in Avondale, 33 miles from Mesa and in state. 7-day money back guarantee and a 190-point inspection. Listed 12 Sep, so 10 days. Avondale tax is 8.8%, the highest city rate on the board, which costs about $110 against Mesa - noise next to the $1,103.
checks: Ask EchoPark for the free CarFax and confirm the one-owner / zero-accident history
EchoPark is no-haggle, so the price is the price - compare out-the-door numbers
Understand the 7-day money back terms: mileage cap, restocking, who pays for what
1.5L turbo oil dilution: smell the dipstick, check the level is not above full
Check open recalls by VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, including 26V332000
Call any Phoenix Honda dealer with the VIN for the free factory service history
Independent pre-purchase inspection, not EchoPark's own 190-point one
